subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should OpenClaw permanently accept `mcp.servers.*.disabled` as a user-facing configuration alias, or retain the documented `enabled: false`-only contract and migrate any legacy files through Doctor?
rationale: The branch changes a public persisted configuration contract rather than only repairing spawn selection, and current repository guidance favors canonical runtime shapes with compatibility conversion in migration/doctor code.

options.title: Keep one canonical setting
options.body: Retain `enabled: false` as the only accepted runtime key and use a scoped Doctor migration if legacy disabled entries require repair.

options.title: Adopt the alias deliberately
options.body: Accept `disabled` as a documented public alias only with defined conflict precedence, full canonicalization, migration behavior, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical setting
recommendation.body: Retain `enabled: false` as the only accepted runtime key and use a scoped Doctor migration if legacy disabled entries require repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged MCP lifecycle work provides the closest visible adjacent ownership signal in the supplied history, though configuration-contract ownership remains uncertain.
